text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- The Social Democratic Party (SPOe) cannot regain absolute majority in Vienna local elections due October, while the conservative People's Party (OeVP) cannot push the Freedom Party off second place, survey finds.
- Tour operator Itas, specialising in Greek holidays, files for bankruptcy with debts of around 1.3 billion schillings making it Austria's largest bankruptcy in the travel industry.
- Hospitalised President Thomas Klestil's condition continues improving, although doctors are still no wiser as to how the president got the virulent strain of pneumonia.
- Austria's budget threatened by high debt burden of municipalities, which last year whipped up debts of 105.7 billion schillings.
- Privatisation of AMAG (Austria Metall AG) with an "Austrian solution" could see employees owning 20 percent of the company.
- Economic research institutes WIFO and IHS stick to their bleak forecasts for Austrian GDP growth.
- Savings bank Die Erste vehemently denies demanding the resignation of Creditanstalt chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari as a prerequisite for its involvement in the privatisation of the bank.
- Tyre maker Semperit Reifen AG, battling against parent company Conti of Germany's plan to halve production at the Traiskirchen plant and slash jobs, presents today its budget for 1997 and 1998.
- Creditanstalt closes down accounts belonging to the Scientology sect.
- Boehler Edelstahl, unit of steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm, reports slight downturn in sales for the first half to 2.375 billion schillings after 2.447 billion in the year-ago period.
